new.descnews: USDA Country of Origin Labeling requires covered fish and shellfish at many retail stores to identify origin and whether the product is wild-caught or farm-raised. Restaurants, some smaller retailers, and processed products can be exempt, so ask when the information is not shown.

Neither production method is automatically better. Wild fisheries differ by stock, gear, bycatch, and management. Farms differ by species, location, siting, feed, water treatment, animal health, and oversight.

source.sourcetitle: NOAA Fisheries — Marine Aquaculture and the Environment

new.descnews: FDA/EPA lists fish as Best Choices, Good Choices, or Choices to Avoid based on mercury for people who are pregnant or breastfeeding and children. Best Choices can be eaten more often than Good Choices under that guidance. Locally caught fish may have separate advisories.

Read beyond a logo or broad word such as “natural” or “sustainable.” Look for the exact standard, scope, certifier, chain-of-custody information, and a public explanation of the assessment. Government stock and advisory links provide useful independent context.

source.sourcetitle: NOAA Fisheries — Seafood Mislabeling and Fraud
